title_en: Huajian Electronics Co., Ltd. and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. v. Guangzhou Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao — dispute over a cooperation agreement
ruling_gist_en: For the purpose of reaching cooperation, the parties entered into multiple contracts, but only one of them contained an arbitration clause. After the arbitral award concerning that contract became effective, a lawsuit was filed due to disputes arising from other contracts without an arbitration clause. If one party asserts that the people's court has no jurisdiction solely on the ground that the arbitral award has taken effect, the people's court shall not support such assertion. In circumstances where the contract on which the effective arbitral award is based differs from the contract on which the people's court handles the dispute, and the content of the people's court's trial does not involve the matters stipulated in the arbitration clause, if one party argues that the people's court should not entertain the case again on the ground of res judicata, the people's court shall not support such argument.

full_text_en:
Huajian Electronic Co., Ltd. and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. v. Guangzhou Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao — Dispute over a Cooperation Agreement

[Ruling Summary]

When parties enter into multiple contracts to achieve a cooperative purpose, but only one contract contains an arbitration clause, and after the arbitration award concerning that contract takes effect, a lawsuit is filed regarding disputes under other contracts that do not contain an arbitration clause, the people's court shall not support a party's claim that the people's court lacks jurisdiction solely on the ground that the arbitration award has taken effect. Where the contract on which the effective arbitration award is based differs from the contract on which the people's court handles the disputed case, and the content under review by the people's court does not involve the matters covered by the arbitration clause, the people's court shall not support a party's claim that the people's court should not re-hear the matter on the ground of "res judicata."

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 10

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huajian Electronic Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Kequn Building, No. 30 Xueyuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Hong Lin, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Yushuang, lawyer of Beijing Huicheng Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd., domiciled at: West Building, Kequn Building, No. 257 Beisihuan Middle Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Hong Lin, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Yushuang, lawyer of Beijing Huicheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guangzhou Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Room C204-1, Area C, Guangzhou International Enterprise Incubator, Science City, Guangzhou High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Feng Mengjue, Chairman of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Liu Jicheng, lawyer of Guangdong Shenglun Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Lu Yuxing, trainee lawyer of Guangdong Shenglun Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xie Xiongping, male, Han Chinese, born on March 8, 1967, residing at: Room 402, No. 60, Changle Yuan, Yuancun Street, Tianhe District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
Agent ad litem: Huang Lisheng, lawyer of Guangdong Global Jingwei Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhang Heping, male, Han Chinese, born on March 15, 1966, registered address: Room 1104, No. 184, Xujing West Street, Tianhe District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, currently residing at: Dormitory of Shunfengshan Huabao Electronics Factory, Daliang, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.
Agent ad litem: Huang Lisheng, lawyer of Guangdong Global Jingwei Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Qiu Shaoming, male, Han Chinese, born on September 12, 1961, registered address: Room 602, No. 49, Lujing East Road, Dengfeng Street, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, currently residing at: Room C204-1, Area C, Guangzhou International Enterprise Incubator, Science City, Guangzhou High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Guangdong Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Huang Ruohao, male, Han Chinese, born on May 25, 1962, registered address: Collective household, Tianhe High-tech Development Zone, Shipai Section, Zhongshan Avenue, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, currently residing at: Room 304, Building 22, No. 108, Shuangbai Lane, Xuanwu District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

In the case of a dispute over a cooperation agreement between the applicants for retrial, Huajian Electronic Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huajian Electronics) and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huajian Translation), and the respondents, Guangzhou Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tech Company), Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, the Guangdong Higher People's Court rendered a civil ruling on June 3, 2008, (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315, which has become legally effective. This Court rendered a civil ruling on July 20, 2009, (2008) Min Shen Zi No. 833, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on May 13, 2010. Wang Yushuang, the agent ad litem of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation; Liu Jicheng and Lu Yuxing, the agents ad litem of Tech Company; and Huang Lisheng, the agent ad litem of Xie Xiongping and Zhang Heping, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. Qiu Shaoming and Huang Ruohao, after being lawfully summoned by this Court, did not appear to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

On August 8, 2006, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation filed a lawsuit with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, stating: In the second half of 2004, due to the unsatisfactory performance of Guangzhou Kuangshi Technology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kuangshi Company) and the downturn of the Hong Kong stock market, the listing process of the overseas subsidiaries of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation stalled. After various considerations, in early 2005, Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, and Tech Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao reached a consensus that there were difficulties in listing in the short term, and agreed to terminate the three agreements already signed, namely, the "Cooperation Agreement", the "Equity Transfer Agreement", and the "Framework Agreement" for Huajian Electronics' introduction of venture capital investors, and to restore Kuangshi Company to its original state. However, Tech Company repeatedly delayed handling the industrial and commercial registration procedures for restoring the equity of Kuangshi Company under various pretexts. At the end of 2005, disregarding the already reached consensus on terminating the cooperation and restoring the equity structure, Tech Company, relying on the current status of the industrial and commercial registration of Kuangshi Company's equity, which had not yet been restored to its original state, unilaterally applied for arbitration based on the "Equity Transfer Agreement". Because the arbitration clause was only stipulated in the "Equity Transfer Agreement", and Tech Company refused to reach an arbitration agreement covering the "Cooperation Agreement" and the "Framework Agreement" as part of the overall cooperation project, the Beijing Arbitration Commission ultimately issued an award holding Huajian Electronics liable for paying the equity transfer price and interest, resulting in adverse consequences for Huajian Electronics. According to Article 3, Clause 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement" entered into by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation and Tech Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, if, for various reasons, the restructuring and listing of Huajian Electronics does not materialize, then this Agreement, the "Equity Transfer Agreement", and the "Framework Agreement" shall be terminated. With respect to the part already performed, the parties agree to restore it to its original state as much as possible, including but not limited to returning the agreed price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-completing corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes. For losses caused to both parties as a result, the parties agree to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness. Tech Company, by severing the overall relationship among the "Cooperation Agreement", the "Framework Agreement", and the "Equity Transfer Agreement", concealing the true background of the equity transfer, and applying for arbitration, seriously violated the stipulations of Article 3, Clause 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement". This act directly forced Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation to initiate this lawsuit to restore the facts and protect their lawful rights and interests, causing them severe economic losses. They requested the people's court: 1. To confirm that the "Cooperation Agreement" is lawful and valid; 2. To order the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement" and to change the registration of the equity of Kuangshi Company held nominally by Huajian Electronics (90%) to be held by Xie Xiongping (36.11%), Huang Ruohao (14.33%), Zhang Heping (14.31%), Qiu Shaoming (0.25%), and Tech Company (25%) respectively, and to change the registration of the equity of Kuangshi Company held nominally by Huajian Translation (10%) to be held by Xie Xiongping; 3. To order Tech Company to compensate Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation for additional economic losses of RMB 166,435.3 caused by its breach of contract, including arbitration legal fees of RMB 50,000, the amount of RMB 48,000 already deducted in the enforcement of the arbitration award by the Haidian District People's Court, Beijing, the arbitration costs borne by Huajian Electronics of RMB 51,630, and the expenses for traveling to Guangzhou for investigation and evidence collection of RMB 16,805.3; 4. To order Tech Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Tech Company responded in its defense, stating: The "Cooperation Agreement" reflects the true intentions of both parties and is lawful and valid. However, the "Cooperation Agreement" was not actually performed; it was merely an expression of the intent to cooperate and had no specific binding force on the parties. Tech Company disagreed with the second claim of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. They did not request the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement", so Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation had no basis to request Tech Company to perform in accordance with Article 3, Clause 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement". Without the termination of the "Equity Transfer Agreement", their second claim could not be sustained.

Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, and Qiu Shaoming jointly responded in their defense at first instance, stating: They agreed with Tech Company's defense opinion, i.e., the "Cooperation Agreement" was merely a letter of intent between the parties, and it was not actually performed. What was actually performed was the "Equity Transfer Agreement". Whether the "Cooperation Agreement" was lawful and valid or not was irrelevant to changing the equity structure. Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation claimed that they did not participate in the operation and planning, but the directors of Kuangshi Company were all appointed by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court found that on December 25, 2003, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, jointly as Party A, and Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Tech Company, jointly as Party B, entered into a "Cooperation Agreement". The agreement stipulated: Parties A and B have reached a cooperative intention regarding equity transfer and investment. Party A intends to acquire all equity of Kuangshi Company held by Party B. At the same time, Party B intends to act as a venture capital investor in Party A's proposed overseas listed company. Party A undertakes that the affiliated company of Party B can obtain shares in the subsidiary of Party A to be listed on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong in accordance with the terms of the "Framework Agreement". To facilitate Party A's listing work, Party B agrees to begin making industrial and commercial changes to Kuangshi Company as required by Party A after the signing of this agreement. However, Party A undertakes that the actual controller of Kuangshi Company before listing shall still be Party B, and its actual owner's equity shall not be changed in any way before listing. If, for various reasons, Party A's restructuring and listing does not materialize, then this Agreement, the "Equity Transfer Agreement", and the "Framework Agreement" shall be terminated. With respect to the part already performed, the parties agree to restore it to its original state as much as possible, including but not limited to returning the agreed price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-completing corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes. For losses caused to both parties as a result, the parties agree to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness.

On the same day as the signing of the above agreement, Huajian Electronics, as Party A, and Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Huang Ruohao, Qiu Shaoming, and Tech Company, as Party B, entered into a "Framework Agreement" for Huajian Electronics' introduction of venture capital investors. The agreement stipulated: Party A intends to restructure its business and list it on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. Party A guarantees that after the share transfer, Party B shall undergo an equity swap; i.e., after the equity swap, Party B shall hold 8% of the equity of Cayman Huajian. However, the final percentage of Cayman Huajian's equity held by Party B shall be determined by the total market capitalization of the company at the time of the offering and the market capitalization amount available for Party B to subscribe, as ultimately confirmed by both Party A and Party B. The transfer price per share between Party A and Party B shall be the issue price when Cayman Huajian lists on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. Party A guarantees that Cayman Huajian will list on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. If the listing does not materialize for various reasons, the "Cooperation Agreement" entered into by Party A and Party B shall be terminated, and all payments already made by Party B shall be returned in the manner specified in the "Cooperation Agreement," and other terms.

On the same day as the signing of the above two agreements, Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Tech Company, jointly as Party A, and Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, jointly as Party B, entered into an "Equity Transfer Agreement". The agreement stipulated: Party A transfers 95% of the equity it holds in Kuangshi Company to Party B. Among them, Tech Company transfers all of the 25% equity it holds in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics. In case of any dispute, it shall be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for resolution. Since the registered capital of Kuangshi Company was RMB 12 million, the amount of registered capital transferred by Tech Company to Huajian Electronics was RMB 3 million. After the above equity transfer, the shareholding structure of Kuangshi Company was: Xie Xiongping's capital contribution amount was RMB 600,000, accounting for 5%; Huajian Electronics' capital contribution amount was RMB 10.8 million, accounting for 90%; Huajian Translation's capital contribution amount was RMB 600,000, accounting for 5%. The parties lawfully handled the equity registration change. On February 2, 2004, Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, and Xie Xiongping held a shareholders' meeting and decided to approve Xie Xiongping's transfer of his 5% capital contribution of RMB 600,000 to Huajian Translation, and handled the industrial and commercial registration change procedures.

On February 5, 2003, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, with Document Guo Han Zi [2001] No. 112, approved and accepted the application of Huajian Electronics for restructuring and overseas listing, and required the company to expedite preparations, fulfill relevant approval procedures in accordance with the requirements of relevant laws, regulations, and rules.

In the second half of 2004, due to various considerations such as company performance and listing timing, the listing process was delayed to some extent. In early 2005, after various considerations, Huajian Electronics and the former shareholders of Kuangshi Company reached a consensus that there were difficulties in listing in the short term and agreed to terminate the signed agreements and sign corresponding termination agreements to restore Kuangshi Company to its original state. In mid-March 2005, Kuangshi Company held a board of directors meeting (attended by former shareholders and shareholder representatives) to collectively discuss matters relating to restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company. At that time, Yang Lin and Shen Kun, representatives of Tech Company, also attended the meeting. After reaching a consensus, all parties agreed to the restoration matter and decided that Kuangshi Company would send a letter to Huajian Electronics requesting cooperation in handling the industrial and commercial registration changes. On April 30, 2005, Huajian Electronics sent the termination agreement it drafted and corresponding documents to Huang Ruohao via email. On February 13, 2006, Huang Ruohao and Zhang Heping issued a declaration and guarantee letter to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, stating: Regardless of whether the "Cooperation Agreement", the "Framework Agreement", and the "Equity Transfer Agreement" signed in December 2003 by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, on the one hand, and Xie Xiongping, Tech Company, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, and Qiu Shaoming, on the other hand, were valid or not, we declare that as of February 13, 2006, the performance of these three agreements is terminated. At the same time, we guarantee not to claim against Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation for the performance of any obligations stipulated in these three agreements. Xie Xiongping also issued a guarantee letter to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, stating: We guarantee not to claim against Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation for the performance of any obligations stipulated in these three agreements.

On December 12, 2005, Tech Company, based on the arbitration clause in the "Equity Transfer Agreement", applied to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration, requesting a ruling that Huajian Electronics pay RMB 3 million as equity transfer price and interest. After hearing the case, the arbitration tribunal held that, since the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement" did not stipulate that the relevant disputes between the parties would be resolved by the Beijing Arbitration Commission, the tribunal suggested that the parties consider whether to submit the disputes under the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement" to the tribunal for joint hearing. However, the parties failed to reach a consensus on this. Accordingly, the tribunal would not hear the potential disputes between the parties based on the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement". The tribunal also noted that Article 125 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law") stipulates that the purpose of the contract should be considered when interpreting a contract. However, due to the existence of the agreed arbitration rules, even if it was discovered that the parties had other complex commercial purposes when signing the "Equity Transfer Agreement", the tribunal had no authority to make a decision beyond its jurisdiction solely based on the purpose of the contract. Consequently, on May 16, 2006, the tribunal issued an arbitration award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474, ruling: 1. Huajian Electronics shall pay RMB 3 million as equity transfer fee to Tech Company; 2. Huajian Electronics shall pay overdue interest of RMB 440,000 to Tech Company and overdue interest from December 1, 2005, until full payment of the equity transfer price (calculated at 0.021% per day). Tech Company, based on the (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 award, applied to the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing for enforcement. The Haidian District People's Court lawfully deducted RMB 48,000 from Huajian Electronics.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held that the "Cooperation Agreement" entered into by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, on the one hand, and Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Tech Company, on the other hand, was the true intention of the parties. The content of the agreement did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations and was a valid agreement. The parties should strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contract. The agreement stipulated: "If, for various reasons, Party A's restructuring and listing does not materialize, then this Agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated. With respect to the part already performed, the parties agree to restore it to its original state as much as possible, including but not limited to returning the agreed price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-completing corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes. For losses caused to both parties as a result, the parties agree to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness." After the signing of the "Cooperation Agreement", Huajian Electronics, as agreed, transferred all equity held by Xie Xiongping (46.11%), Huang Ruohao (14.33%), Zhang Heping (14.31%), Qiu Shaoming (0.25%), and Tech Company (25%) in Kuangshi Company to be registered as 90% held by Huajian Electronics and 10% held by Huajian Translation. The purpose of Huajian Electronics in signing the above agreement and making the equity registration change was to fulfill the requirements of the China Securities Regulatory Commission to expedite preparations and complete relevant approval procedures. Due to various reasons such as company performance and listing timing, the indirect overseas listing of Huajian Electronics was not completed. Regarding the failure of the listing, Huajian Electronics had notified the former shareholders of Kuangshi Company and requested the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement". Tech Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao did not cooperate with Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation in performing the obligation of industrial and commercial registration changes as agreed to restore the original equity status of Kuangshi Company. Their actions constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach. Therefore, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation's claim, based on the failure of Tech Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao to perform their obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement", requesting the complete change of registration of their respective 90% and 10% equity in Kuangshi Company to the names of Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Tech Company should be supported.

The Equity Transfer Agreement signed by Huajian Electronics Company, Huajian Translation Company, and Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao contained an arbitration clause and was arbitrated by the Beijing Arbitration Commission, with the arbitral award having already taken legal effect. Since Huajian Electronics Company was required to transfer its 25% equity in Kuangshi Company to Technology Company’s name, Technology Company’s receipt of the equity transfer payment of RMB 48,000 lacked a legal basis, and Technology Company should return this amount to Huajian Electronics Company. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company claimed additional economic losses caused by Technology Company’s breach of contract, including an arbitration attorney fee of RMB 50,000, an arbitration fee of RMB 51,630 that Huajian Electronics Company was obligated to bear, and investigation and evidence collection expenses of RMB 16,805.3 for a trip to Guangzhou, totaling RMB 118,435.3. As these losses did not have a necessary causal relationship with the present case, the claim by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company for compensation for these losses was untenable and not supported. On August 23, 2007, the Guangzhou Intermediate People’s Court rendered the civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220, holding: 1. The Cooperation Agreement signed in December 2003 between Huajian Electronics Company, Huajian Translation Company, and Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company is dissolved. 2. Within one month from the effective date of this judgment, Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company shall assist Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company in registering the transfer of the respective 90% and 10% equity interests held by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company in Kuangshi Company to the names of Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, with Xie Xiongping holding 46.11%, Huang Ruohao holding 14.33%, Zhang Heping holding 14.31%, Qiu Shaoming holding 0.25%, and Technology Company holding 25%. 3. Within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, Technology Company shall return RMB 48,000 to Huajian Electronics Company. 4. The other claims of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 70,842 shall be borne jointly by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company in the amount of RMB 690; and by Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company in the amount of RMB 70,152 in proportion to their respective shareholdings.

Technology Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: 1. The termination condition stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement is not a genuine condition, and the first-instance court’s determination that the condition was fulfilled was unsupported, thus the dissolution of the Cooperation Agreement lacked factual basis. 2. The first-instance judgment disregarded the effective arbitral award and, without dissolving, revoking, or confirming the invalidity of the Equity Transfer Agreement, directly ordered the restoration of equity, seriously violating the principle of "res judicata." If this judgment takes effect, it would conflict with the arbitral award, undermining judicial authority. Terminating the Cooperation Agreement cannot produce the legal consequence of restoring equity proportions, and the first-instance judgment ordering restoration of equity had no legal basis. The Beijing Arbitration Commission’s award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 had already found the following facts: The Equity Transfer Agreement (transferring 95% equity) was actually performed; the agreement was valid and legally binding; Technology Company had the right to demand continued performance, i.e., to demand that Huajian Electronics Company pay RMB 3 million in equity transfer consideration and liquidated damages. Huajian Electronics Company’s application to the Beijing Second Intermediate People’s Court to set aside the arbitral award had been dismissed. However, in this case, Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company sought to terminate the Cooperation Agreement and restore equity, and according to Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, the legal consequence of restoring equity arises only if the Cooperation Agreement, the Equity Transfer Agreement, and the Framework Agreement are terminated simultaneously, not as a consequence of performing the Cooperation Agreement. The Cooperation Agreement itself does not address the specifics of equity transfer; merely terminating the Cooperation Agreement cannot produce the legal consequence of restoring equity proportions. The first-instance court, in its judgment, did not address the Equity Transfer Agreement (transferring 95% equity) or confirm its invalidity, yet directly ordered the restoration of equity proportions and required Technology Company to return amounts received under the effective arbitral award, which was entirely erroneous.

Zhang Heping, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: 1. The first-instance judgment severed the connections among the Cooperation Agreement, the Equity Transfer Agreement, and the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company’s claim was to terminate the Cooperation Agreement and transfer 36.11% equity held by Huajian Electronics Company and 10% equity held by Huajian Translation Company to Zhang Heping’s name, but they did not simultaneously seek to dissolve the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract. The Cooperation Agreement was merely a letter of intent between Zhang Heping and Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company; the documents that specifically defined the rights and obligations of both parties were the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract. The document registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce was the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract, not the Cooperation Agreement. In 2003 and 2004, Zhang Heping transferred his 46.11% equity in the company in question to Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company pursuant to the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract, and Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company did not seek to dissolve the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Capital Contribution Transfer Contract. Therefore, the equity could not be returned to Zhang Heping under the Cooperation Agreement. 2. The first-instance judgment improperly applied the law, cited contradictory legal provisions, and its content exceeded the claims of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company. They sought termination, not dissolution, of the Cooperation Agreement, but the first-instance judgment went beyond their claim. 3. The Beijing Arbitration Commission’s effective award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 ordered Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company to pay RMB 3 million in equity transfer consideration to Technology Company, and the award had taken effect and been executed. However, the first-instance judgment overturned the arbitral award with its decision, seriously violating the law. In summary, the first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and improper application of law, and he requested the court of second instance to set aside items 1 and 2 of the first-instance judgment and dismiss the claims of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company.

Xie Xiongping and Qiu Shaoming also appealed the first-instance judgment, with the same grounds as Zhang Heping.

Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company responded jointly in the second instance, arguing that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and the appeals of Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Zhang Heping were without merit; they requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeals.

The Guangdong High People’s Court, upon trial, confirmed that the facts found by the first-instance court were essentially true.

It was also found that: In December 2003, Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao signed the Equity Transfer Agreement with Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company, agreeing to transfer all equity in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company, and Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company would pay RMB 12 million in equity transfer consideration to Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao.

Huajian Electronics Company, believing that the Beijing Arbitration Commission’s award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 was factually erroneous, applied to the Beijing Second Intermediate People’s Court to set it aside. On October 27, 2006, the Beijing Second Intermediate People’s Court issued the civil ruling (2006) Er Zhong Min Te Zi No. 12426, dismissing Huajian Electronics Company’s application to set aside the arbitral award.

The Guangdong High People’s Court held that the Cooperation Agreement, the Framework Agreement, and the Equity Transfer Agreement signed by Huajian Electronics Company, Huajian Translation Company, and Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao concerning the equity transfer of Kuangshi Company were all genuine expressions of the parties’ intent, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and the equity in Kuangshi Company had been registered under the names of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company. Therefore, all these contracts were valid and legally binding on the parties.

After these contracts were signed, Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao transferred their equity in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company in accordance with the contract terms and had the relevant equity registered under the names of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company. On December 12, 2005, Technology Company applied to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration, claiming that Huajian Electronics Company had breached the Equity Transfer Agreement by failing to pay the equity transfer consideration. On May 16, 2006, the Beijing Arbitration Commission issued the award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474, ordering Huajian Electronics Company to pay Technology Company RMB 3 million in equity transfer consideration, RMB 440,000 in overdue interest, and overdue interest from December 1, 2005, until full payment of the equity transfer consideration. Huajian Electronics Company, dissatisfied with the award, applied to the Beijing Second Intermediate People’s Court to set it aside, but the application was dismissed. Now, Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company filed a lawsuit with the people’s court against Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao pursuant to the Cooperation Agreement, seeking termination of the Cooperation Agreement and registration of the Kuangshi Company equity under the names of Technology Company and Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao. Although the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement provided that if Huajian Electronics Company’s overseas subsidiary failed to list in Hong Kong, then the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement should be terminated and the equity in Kuangshi Company should be restored to the names of Technology Company and Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, the arbitral tribunal did not rule on the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement. In this case, the Cooperation Agreement, the Framework Agreement, and the Equity Transfer Agreement form an indivisible whole, and the people’s court should hear all of these agreements together. However, since the arbitral tribunal had already ruled on the Equity Transfer Agreement, ordering Huajian Electronics Company to pay Technology Company RMB 3 million in equity transfer consideration and overdue interest, the people’s court’s acceptance of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company’s claims for termination of the Cooperation Agreement and registration of the Kuangshi Company equity under the names of Technology Company and Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao necessarily involved the Equity Transfer Agreement, which had already been adjudicated by the arbitral tribunal. Therefore, the claims of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company would inevitably conflict with the arbitral award. The first-instance court’s judgment dissolving the Cooperation Agreement and restoring the Kuangshi Company equity held by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company to the names of Technology Company and Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao contradicted the content of the arbitral award in question and essentially re-adjudicated matters that had been decided by the arbitral tribunal, violating the principle of "res judicata." The first-instance court’s acceptance of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company’s lawsuit and issuance of a substantive judgment was improper and should be corrected in accordance with the law. On June 3, 2008, the Guangdong High People’s Court issued the civil ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315, setting aside the civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People’s Court and dismissing the lawsuit of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company. The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees of RMB 50 each were to be borne by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company.

Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, Paragraph 1, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Procedure Law"), requesting the reversal of the civil ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315 of the Guangdong High People’s Court and the upholding of the civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People’s Court of Guangdong Province. The main reasons were as follows:

(1) The lawsuit filed by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company satisfied the statutory conditions, and neither of the two contracts on which the lawsuit was based contained an arbitration clause. Therefore, the people’s court should accept the case and conduct substantive trial. The Guangdong High People’s Court’s dismissal of the lawsuit pursuant to Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law constituted an error in the application of law.

(2) The trial of this case by the people’s court did not conflict with the Beijing Arbitration Commission’s award. The dispute among the parties concerning the restoration of the equity structure of Kuangshi Company under the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, and the dispute concerning the payment of equity transfer consideration under the Equity Transfer Agreement, involved different legal relationships and did not fall within the circumstances to which the principle of "res judicata" applies. The Guangdong High People’s Court’s application of that principle in the second-instance ruling was a clear error in the application of law.

(3) Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company’s lawsuit based on the valid Cooperation Agreement and Framework Agreement was dismissed by the people’s court, while the arbitral tribunal, when hearing the Equity Transfer Agreement, did not address the Cooperation Agreement or the Framework Agreement. This left no avenue for the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company.

Technology Company responded, arguing that the people’s court did indeed have the authority to hear the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement. However, because the termination condition stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement was not fulfilled in this case, the people’s court could not find that the Cooperation Agreement and related agreements should be terminated based on that, and certainly could not directly render a judgment restoring the equity structure.

Xie Xiongping and Zhang Heping responded, arguing that although the people’s court had jurisdiction over the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Investment Agreement, if the people’s court found Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement to be valid, then the judgment would necessarily conflict with the effective arbitral award, violating the principle of "res judicata."

This Court, upon retrial, confirmed that the facts found by the first-instance and second-instance courts were the same.

This Court held that, based on the reasons for the parties’ application for retrial and the responses, the issues in dispute in this case were as follows:

I. Whether this case falls under the jurisdiction of the people’s court.

The Guangdong High People’s Court dismissed the lawsuit of Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company pursuant to Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company applied for retrial, arguing that neither of the two contracts on which they based their lawsuit contained an arbitration clause, so the people’s court should accept the case and conduct substantive trial. After this Court held a hearing, the respondents, Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, and Zhang Heping, also considered that the people’s court had jurisdiction over this case.

This Court held that the lawsuit filed by Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company was based on the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, neither of which contained an arbitration clause. The arbitral award explicitly stated, "The arbitral tribunal shall not hear any possible disputes between the parties arising from the Framework Agreement and the Cooperation Agreement." Therefore, this case falls under the jurisdiction of the people’s court. The Guangdong High People’s Court’s reliance on Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law to find that this case did not fall under the jurisdiction of the people’s court was an error in the application of law, which this Court corrects in accordance with the law.

II. Whether Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement is invalid and whether the termination condition stipulated therein has been fulfilled.

Technology Company argued that Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, which provided that "if for any reason Party A’s restructuring and listing is unsuccessful, then this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated," constituted a conditional termination clause, but the condition "if for any reason Party A’s restructuring and listing is unsuccessful" was not a genuine condition, and the provision was therefore invalid. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company argued that the provision did not violate mandatory provisions of law and should be valid.

This Court held that the basis for finding a contract or a condition in a contract to be invalid is Article 52 of the Contract Law. The condition in Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement did not violate the provisions of Article 52 of the Contract Law regarding the invalidity of contracts and should be found valid as a matter of law. Since the contract is valid, it should be strictly performed in accordance with the content of Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement. If the condition "if for any reason Party A’s restructuring and listing is unsuccessful" has been fulfilled, then "this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated." In this case, although a series of actions were taken by the parties, especially Huajian Electronics Company, it was an objective fact that Huajian Electronics Company’s overseas subsidiary ultimately failed to list in Hong Kong, which matched the parties’ agreement, i.e., "if for any reason Party A’s restructuring and listing is unsuccessful." Therefore, the condition for terminating the Cooperation Agreement and other contracts had been fulfilled. Thus, the first-instance court’s finding that "Huajian Electronics Company had notified the original shareholders of Kuangshi Company of the failure to list and requested termination of the Cooperation Agreement. The five defendants failed to assist the two plaintiffs in fulfilling the obligation to register the change with the industry and commerce administration and restore the original equity structure of Kuangshi Company in accordance with the agreement, constituting a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach. Therefore, the two plaintiffs’ request, based on the five defendants’ failure to perform the obligations under the Cooperation Agreement, to transfer all of their respective 90% and 10% equity interests in Kuangshi Company to the names of the defendants Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company, is supported" was consistent with the parties’ agreement and the law, and this Court upholds it accordingly. According to the Cooperation Agreement, the parties were to restore the Equity Transfer Agreement that had been performed to its original state, with Huajian Electronics Company returning its 25% equity in Kuangshi Company to Technology Company, and Technology Company returning the consideration for the transfer of that equity, including the RMB 48,000, to Huajian Electronics Company.

III. Whether the first-instance court’s judgment restoring the equity to its original state violated the principle of "res judicata" and conflicted with the arbitral award.

Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, and Zhang Heping all believe that the arbitration award has already ruled: (1) Huajian Electronics Company shall pay Technology Company the equity transfer fee of RMB 3,000,000; (2) Huajian Electronics Company shall pay Technology Company overdue payment interest of RMB 440,000 and overdue payment interest from December 1, 2005 to the date of full settlement of the equity transfer payment (calculated at a daily rate of 0.021%). If the people's court were to order the restoration of the equity to its original state, it would violate the principle of "res judicata" and contradict the arbitration award. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company argue that the dispute between the parties regarding the restoration of the equity structure of Kuangshi Company to its original state pursuant to the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, and the dispute between the parties regarding the payment of the equity transfer price for Kuangshi Company under the Equity Transfer Agreement, involve different legal relationships and do not fall within the circumstances prescribed by the principle of "res judicata." The trial of this case by the people's court does not contradict the award of the Beijing Arbitration Commission.

This Court holds that the first instance court's judgment ordering the restoration of equity to its original state did not violate the principle of "res judicata." The reasoning is as follows: Because the "restructuring and listing was not realized," the dispute between Huajian Electronics Company, Huajian Translation Company, and the other parties regarding the restoration of the equity structure of Kuangshi Company to its original state pursuant to Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, and the dispute regarding the payment of the equity transfer price for Kuangshi Company under the Equity Transfer Agreement, involve different legal relationships. They are different claims made by the parties based on different legal facts. According to the terms of the Cooperation Agreement, the performance of the agreement is divided into two phases. The first phase is for the successful restructuring and listing of Huajian Electronics Company's overseas subsidiaries, involving the transfer of Kuangshi Company's equity and payment of the equity transfer price. The second phase is that if the "restructuring and listing is not realized," the equity structure of Kuangshi Company shall be restored to its original state and the transfer price shall be returned. To perform the matters agreed upon in the first phase, the parties further entered into the Equity Transfer Agreement, which contains an arbitration clause excluding the jurisdiction of the people's court. That dispute has already been arbitrated by the Beijing Arbitration Commission. However, to perform the matters agreed upon in the second phase, namely, "If for various reasons Party A's restructuring and listing is not realized, this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated. For the parts already performed, both parties agree to restore them to their original state to the extent possible, including but not limited to returning the agreement price, restoring Kuangshi Technology's equity structure, re-conducting corresponding industrial and commercial changes, etc. For losses caused to both parties thereby, both parties agree to bear them according to the principle of fairness," Huajian Electronics Company filed the lawsuit based on this clause. This case resolves the dispute arising from the performance of the second phase of the Cooperation Agreement. Because the first instance court's basis for handling this case is not the Equity Transfer Agreement but Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, while the arbitration is based on the Equity Transfer Agreement and not Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, and because the agreement underlying the arbitration award differs from the agreement underlying the first instance court's handling of this case, it follows that the first instance court did not handle the dispute arising from the parties' performance of the Equity Transfer Agreement. The arbitration award also explicitly stated that it would not include the Cooperation Agreement within the scope of arbitration. In other words, the "res" (matter) handled by the arbitration award, i.e., the dispute arising from the Equity Transfer Agreement, was not handled by the people's court. Therefore, the first instance court's judgment ordering the restoration of equity to its original state did not violate the principle of "res judicata."

Given that the first instance court's judgment ordering the restoration of equity to its original state did not violate the principle of "res judicata," there is no issue of whether the judgment contradicts the arbitration award. Even if the result of the arbitration award is the performance of the Equity Transfer Agreement, and the result of the judgment is the restoration of Kuangshi Company's equity structure, the judgment was made pursuant to the terms of Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement. That clause still represents the true intent of both parties, including Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao. In other words, both the first instance judgment and the arbitration award were made based on the true intent of the parties, and both are inevitable results of the parties' performance of the agreements. Stated differently, the true intent of the parties was that, for the purpose of restructuring and listing, the equity change of Kuangshi Company should first be carried out, and indeed such an equity change was actually carried out. However, if the listing was not realized, the already changed equity should be restored to its original state. Under the circumstance that the listing was not realized, the first instance court's judgment ordering the restoration of Kuangshi Company's equity structure should be upheld in accordance with the law.

In conclusion, pursuant to the provisions of Article 186, paragraph 1, and Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315 of the Guangdong High People's Court is set aside.

2. The civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
